Publish the package on GitHub

Source: GITHUB_SETUP.md

You do not need a CRAN submission, a package website, or a compiled binary. GitHub can host the package source, and remotes::install_github() builds and installs it on your computer.

Prepare the folder once

  1. Extract the ZIP. The folder containing DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, and R/ is the package root.
  2. Open niceSMD.Rproj in RStudio.
  3. Run the following from that folder:
source("tools/configure_package.R")
source("tools/install_local.R")
source("inst/examples/quickstart.R")
source("tools/check_package.R")

The configuration script asks for your author name, email, GitHub username, and desired repository name. It replaces the clearly marked author email and installation placeholders and adds the repository URLs to DESCRIPTION. It does not connect to GitHub or publish files.

The placeholder email is syntactically valid so the starter has complete package metadata, but replace it with your chosen contact address before publishing. Your GitHub-provided noreply email is also an option.

Confirm that the example Word files open correctly and that the checks pass before relying on the package for an analysis. VALIDATION.md explains the checks that could not be run when this ZIP was prepared.

Option A Upload through the GitHub website

  1. Sign in to GitHub.
  2. Create a repository named niceSMD, or the name chosen during configuration.
  3. Choose public or private visibility. Do not initialize it with a README, license, or .gitignore; these files are already in the package folder.
  4. Choose uploading an existing file or Add file > Upload files.
  5. Upload the contents of the package folder. DESCRIPTION must appear at the repository root, not inside an extra niceSMD/ directory. Uploading just the ZIP will not make the repository installable as an R package.
  6. Include .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml if the browser’s upload dialog omits hidden folders. You can create it with Add file > Create new file, type that exact path, and paste in the supplied YAML contents.
  7. Commit the files. Check the Actions tab for the R package check results.

The .gitignore, .Rbuildignore, and .github entries begin with a dot. On macOS, Command + Shift + Period shows them in Finder. On Windows, enable hidden items in File Explorer. The Git method below includes them automatically.

Do not upload the generated output/ folder or personal datasets.

Option B Push with Git

Create the empty repository first. Then open a terminal in the package root:

git init
git add .
git commit -m "Add initial niceSMD package"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/hyejung0/niceSMD.git
git push -u origin main

Use your actual repository URL if its name differs. Authenticate with GitHub’s normal browser, credential-manager, or SSH flow. Do not put a token in the remote URL or commit it to any file. If git commit requests your identity, configure your local Git author name and email first.

The supplied workflow has read-only repository permissions. It installs dependencies and runs R CMD check, examples, and tests on current R releases for Linux, Windows, and macOS. It does not publish a release or modify code. Workflow files may need enabling in the repository’s Actions settings.

Install from your repository

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("hyejung0/niceSMD")
library(niceSMD)

For a private repository, provide an appropriate GitHub token through your normal environment or credential manager. remotes reads GITHUB_PAT:

# Check whether a token is available without printing its contents:
nzchar(Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT"))
remotes::install_github("hyejung0/niceSMD")

Never place a real token in the repository, README, scripts, or shared output.

Release versions and later updates

The first version is 0.1.0. After checks pass, you may create a GitHub release with tag v0.1.0. A tag lets you reinstall the same source version later:

remotes::install_github("hyejung0/niceSMD@v0.1.0")

When updating, edit the code and relevant tests/help, increase Version in DESCRIPTION, update NEWS.md, rerun checks, and commit/push. Install the updated main branch with remotes::install_github(..., force = TRUE). Restart R before reinstalling if a loaded package cannot be replaced.

No GitHub account is connected and nothing is published merely by extracting or running the package examples.
